subject: Deterministic throughput test matrix and measurement definitions (RFI)
messages:
From: John Doe <j.doe@acme.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Performance Team <perf@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: RFI: deterministic throughput matrix and measurement defs

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for taking this RFI. To move our procurement evaluation forward we need a deterministic throughput/latency matrix you can produce for Redwood in-scope models. Specifically we need:

- Exact measurement definitions (latency percentiles to report, how you measure token vs request latency)
- Test cases: sequence lengths, prompt/continuation ratios, batch sizes and model variants
- Methodology for deterministic load generation (seeding, replay vs synthetic)
- How caching (prefix/KV) is represented in your results and its effect on tail behavior
- Expected QPS scaling curves and where you observe saturation/failure modes

We attached the current RFI packet for context (rfi-acme-2028.pdf). Ideally we would get a matrix that maps traffic shapes to expected p50/p90/p95/p99 at several target SLOs and a short description of the test harness. We may ask you to run a short canary in our staging environment afterward.

Can you confirm you can produce this and provide an estimated delivery timeline?

Thanks,
John
John Doe
Head of Performance Engineering
Acme Corporation

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <j.doe@acme.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: RFI: deterministic throughput matrix and measurement defs

John —

Appreciate the clear ask and attached RFI. Yes, we can produce the deterministic throughput/latency matrix you described. High-level plan and deliverables:

- Deliverable: "Deterministic Throughput Matrix v1" (XLSX) mapping traffic shapes to p50/p90/p95/p99 and sustained throughput at target SLOs.
- Measurement definitions: request latency (request in → last token emitted), token latency (time per token where applicable), and end-to-end wall-clock for multi-token responses. We will report p50/p90/p95/p99 for both request and token latencies.
- Test harness: open-source load generator + deterministic seed files and replay driver. We will provide the harness and a synthetic seed corpus.
- Test cases: short (8–32 tokens), medium (64–128), long (512+), and conversational mixes (prompt:continuation ratios of 1:1, 1:4).
- Cache handling: runs with cold cache, warmed prefix cache (controlled seed), and full-KV-cache-enabled scenarios. We will flag when caching materially changes tail percentiles.
- Environments: default run on Dedicated GPU type (A100 40GB) and quantized variants where applicable — we will include machine specs in the matrix.

I attached an initial spreadsheet skeleton (redwood-deterministic-matrix-v1.xlsx). If this meets your needs we can schedule a 45-min call to align on traffic shapes and approve a canary run in your staging. Proposed ETA for V1 spreadsheet: 3 business days after we confirm the traffic shapes.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0147

From: Acme Performance Team <perf@acme.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Doe <j.doe@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: RFI: deterministic throughput matrix and measurement defs

Hi Lauren,

Thanks — couple of clarifying points before you lock V1: we need the matrix to reflect our real-world traffic shapes, which include:

- Heavy tail of short queries (customer search), occasional long responses (report generation). We will provide a sample distribution file; please indicate how you will map it to your seed corpus.
- We need explicit p99.9 and p99.99 for request latency for cold-cache vs warmed-cache scenarios — our SREs focus on these quantiles.
- Please include tests that demonstrate prefix-cache effectiveness: repeated prefixes vs unique prefixes.
- For scaling curves, we require QPS ramp tests (linear ramp and step-ramp) with identification of first-error modes (queueing, OOM, replica saturation) and guidance on scaling knobs (autoscale policy recommendations).

Finally, we would like Redwood to run one short canary (1 hour) in our staging cluster (we will provide access) using the approved seed set and the same GPU types we run in prod. Can you confirm you will run canary and provide the run artifacts (raw logs, perf counters, and the matrix)?

Regards,
Alex (on behalf of John)
Performance Engineering
Acme Corporation

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Performance Team <perf@acme.com>, John Doe <j.doe@acme.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 11:00:00 +0000
Subject: Re: RFI: deterministic throughput matrix and measurement defs

Alex / John —

Thanks for the clarifications, that level of fidelity is reasonable. Below is our proposed test checklist, measurement definitions, and schedule. If you confirm the traffic-distribution file we will lock the seed set and begin the runs.

Measurement definitions (what we'll report):
- Request latency (ms): time from request received to final token emitted, reported at p50/p90/p95/p99/p99.9/p99.99.
- Token latency (ms): average per-token emission latency for autoregressive responses, reported at p50/p90/p95/p99.
- Throughput: sustained successful requests per second (RPS) at each SLO threshold (e.g., % of requests meeting X ms).
- Error modes: classification and timestamps for errors (timeouts, queue rejects, OOMs).

Test matrix axes and cases:
- Sequence length buckets: S (8–32), M (64–128), L (256–512), XL (512+).
- Mixes: search-heavy (80% S, 15% M, 5% L), mixed (40/40/20), long-tail (65% S, 25% M, 10% XL).
- Cache states: cold, warmed-prefix (repeat prefixes), warmed-kv (full KV cache).
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8; and continuous batching policy (latency target knobs).
- Model variants: open 7B baseline, quantized 7B int8, 13B fp16 (if requested).

Load generation and determinism:
- Seed corpus: we will accept your distribution file and map to deterministic seeds; the harness supports replay with a fixed RNG seed.
- Ramp profile: 5-minute linear warm-up, step ramps to target QPS for 15–30 minutes per level, and a final 2-hour soak at target. For canary: 1 hour soak at agreed QPS.
- Warm-up policy: automated warm-up to populate caches, then cold-run variants executed separately.

Environment & telemetry:
- Hardware: A100 40GB (primary), optional runs on T4 for cost-sensitivity.
- Runtime: Redwood serving engine v4.2 with continuous batching and KV cache enabled.
- Telemetry: token-level timing, per-replica CPU/GPU utilization, queue lengths, paging/OOM counters, and tracer spans. Raw logs and perf counters will be delivered as compressed artifacts.

Artifacts delivered:
- Deterministic Throughput Matrix v1 (XLSX) with raw percentiles and summary charts.
- Raw logs and aggregated perf counters (CSV/JSON).
- A short runbook describing scaling knobs, observed failure modes, and recommended autoscale policy for your expected traffic shapes.

Schedule (proposed):
- Day 0: Confirm traffic distribution file + staging access for canary.
- Days 1–2: Seed mapping, harness configuration, and internal dry runs.
- Day 3: Full deterministic runs and artifact assembly — deliver V1.
- Day 4: If requested, canary run in your staging (1 hour) and delivery of canary artifacts.

Next steps: please upload the traffic distribution file to the Drive link below and we will schedule the alignment call. Once you confirm, we'll assign an engineer and lock the ETA.

Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/file/deterministic-matrix-v1

Cheers,
Lauren
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
